newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banamex, Bancomer unload 16 bln pesos in bad loans.
newsitem.headline: Banamex, Bancomer unload 16 bln pesos in bad loans.

text.p: Banamex and Bancomer, Mexico's two largest banks, each agreed to sell 8.0 billion pesos worth of past-due loans to the special government program known as Fobaproa, the National Bank and Securities Commission (CNBV) said on Thursday.
The two banks agreed to increase capital by 4.0 billion pesos each in exchange for unloading the bad loans.
These were the last operations by Banamex and Bancomer before Dec. 31, 1996, the cut-off date for banks to reach a deal with Fobaproa on their past-due loans, the CNBV said.
Fobaproa was created to bail out banks following the banking crisis caused by the December 1994 peso devaluation.
Aside from Banamex and Bancomer, the banks Bancrecer, Bital and Atlantico also reached agreements with Fobaproa on handing over past-due loans before the cut-off date, the CNBV said.
However, the CNBV did not report the value of loans that those banks sold to Fobaproa.
With these final operations, the net amount of past-due loans taken over by Fobaproa totalled 119.9 billion in the life the program, and the gross total was 142.6 billion pesos, the CNBV said.

In exchange, banks agreed to increase capital by a total of 63.6 billion pesos, an amount equal to 157.5 percent of the accountable capital in the Mexican banking system in the month of December 1994, the CNBV said.
